operator.dynamic_viscosity: Each endpoint dynamic viscosity is restDensity times kinematicViscosity. The interface coefficient is their harmonic combination and is zero when either endpoint is inviscid.
operator.particle_volume: Each endpoint uses explicit restParticleVolume when positive and cubic particle diameter otherwise. Pair volume is the harmonic combination.
operator.traction: Relative velocity is projected onto the retained interface tangent plane. The common pair force is harmonicDynamicViscosity times harmonicParticleVolume times max(1 - distance/maxSupport, 0) times tangentialRelativeVelocity.
operator.balance: The same common force is divided by endpoint particle mass with opposite signs. Enabled acceleration limits clamp the common force before either mass division.
operator.interface_policy: Traction requires two resolved, non-degenerate interface samples and a finite nonzero combined normal. Normal relative motion creates no viscous traction.
operator.advertisement: No interaction capability was added or enabled. Public graph scheduling remains P1-13 and qualification remains P1-14.

physical_fixtures.analytic_sweeps: Three unequal density, explicit volume, particle-mass, support-radius and viscosity pairs match the closed-form harmonic tangential force and inverse-mass endpoint accelerations.
physical_fixtures.momentum: Every active material sweep and the acceleration-limit case conserve mass-weighted linear force within 5e-5 of exchanged-force activity.
physical_fixtures.dissipation: Instantaneous pair power is strictly negative for every active shear fixture.
physical_fixtures.normal_no_mixing: Pure interface-normal relative motion produces exactly zero added acceleration at both endpoints.
physical_fixtures.zero_and_invalid_limits: Either inviscid endpoint, a missing interface sample, or a degenerate interface sample produces exactly zero traction.
physical_fixtures.endpoint_reversal: Swapping endpoint populations and materials while reversing oriented interface normals preserves each physical particle acceleration.
physical_fixtures.bounded_force: Unequal endpoint masses respect both requested maximum pair accelerations while preserving common-force balance.
